newsitem.title: USA: Cyprus Amax lost more than $50 million in quarter.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus Amax lost more than $50 million in quarter.

text.p: Cyprus Amax Minerals Co. Wednesday reported a loss of more than $50 million in the fourth quarter due to sharply lower copper and molybdenum prices.
The company said it lost $52 million, or 61 cents a share, on sales of $754 million, compared with a profit of $96 million or 93 cents a share on sales of $739 million, a year earlier.
Cyprus said its results were also pressured by a charge of $61 million to temporarily suspend operations at its Tohono mine near Casa Grande, Ariz., to correct environmental problems.
It said its copper and molybdenum operations lost $37 million in the fourth quarter compared with a profit of $120 million in 1995.
The company said its copper prices averaged $1.01 a pound during the quarter, down from $1.30 a year earlier, and molybdenum prices averaged $5.23 a pound vs. $5.87 a pound.
The coal unit earned $24 million, down from $35 million.

"We will be producing one billion pounds of copper in 1997, some 35 to 40 per cent of this from our low cost South American operations," said Milton H. Ward, chairman and chief executive officer. Last year, Cyprus produced 767 million pounds of copper.
Cyprus Amax's stock was off 25 cents at $23.25 on the New York Stock Exchange.
